summary: PRODUCTION acceptance pass executed against LIVE https://cargoone.co.uk. Section 1 deployment sanity (api/, www→apex 308, SPA deep-link 200, strict CORS with credentials, TLS) — PASS. Section 2 full auth on production incl. HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Lax+Path=/ session cookie, host-only (no explicit Domain), zero JWT/token keys in localStorage/sessionStorage post-login (only PostHog), logout clears session, unauth /api/auth/me→401, bad login controlled error, duplicate register 400/409, hard-refresh /customer restores session — PASS. Section 3 RBAC customer→/admin and customer→/driver both bounce back to /customer via UI, backend blocks with 401/403 — PASS. Section 4 marketing pages (/how-it-works, /services, /business, /drivers, /faq, /contact, /trust-safety, /about) all 200, mobile 390px homepage horizontal overflow 0 — PASS. Section 8 full cross-role E2E completed on production with fresh disposable accounts: customer created bidding job London→Manchester (£200 budget), admin approved disposable driver via POST /api/admin/users/{id}/approve, driver submitted £150 bid, customer accepted bid then created booking; all IDs captured. Section 9 data-consistency assertion booking.customer_id / booking.driver_id match disposable users — PASS. Section 12 negatives (invalid booking id → 404, bad login → 401, unauth me → 401, wrong-role → 401/403) — PASS. Baseline backend regression NOT re-run (per instructions honour the 221p/16f/8e/1s baseline as-is). Two very small items to flag (not blockers).

minor.issue: Response body still returns access_token JWT in JSON alongside setting the HttpOnly cookie. Frontend correctly does NOT persist it (localStorage / sessionStorage only contain PostHog keys post-login), but exposing the JWT in the response body means any 3rd-party script that later runs on cargoone.co.uk could scrape it from the login XHR. Recommend either omitting access_token from the JSON response once cookie auth is in place, or gating it behind a mobile-client header. Non-blocking for web launch.

action_items: P3-info: Consider removing access_token from the JSON body of POST /api/auth/login now that the HttpOnly cookie is the source of truth on web. Frontend already ignores it so removal is a low-risk hardening.
critical_code_review_comments: Session cookie configured correctly: HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax + Path=/ + host-only (no Domain attribute) as required by acceptance spec.
CORS is strict — explicit https://cargoone.co.uk allow-origin plus allow-credentials=true; no wildcard.
www→apex handled at edge with 308 + HSTS max-age=63072000 includeSubDomains preload — production-grade.
SPA fallback on /customer/*, /driver/*, /admin/*, /driver-profile/*, /settings/*, /auth/* all return 200 HTML — Kubernetes ingress + Cloudflare correctly routing non-/api paths to the React bundle.
Backend enforces role gates at the API layer (customer & driver receive 401/403 on /api/admin/users), matching UI redirects — defence in depth.
Job-post endpoint requires pickup_town, dropoff_town, collection_date, delivery_date — payload contract is stable and matches the wizard used in the customer portal.
Bid endpoint enforces driver.status == 'active' before allowing POST /api/jobs/{id}/bids — matches admin approve flow.
Accept bid + create booking is a two-step call (POST /api/bids/{id}/accept then POST /api/bookings {job_id}) which is what the customer portal already does.

rca_of_the_issue: No production-blocking defect discovered in this acceptance pass. The one P3-info item (login JSON body still contains access_token) is a leftover from the mobile-app era of the codebase; on web the HttpOnly cookie is what actually authenticates subsequent calls, and the frontend does not persist the returned token (confirmed via localStorage/sessionStorage inspection = only PostHog keys). Removing it from the web login response is a small backend change and requires redeploy — deferred to owner decision.
